reconcile.note: Henry sequences the angel's appearances, having him sit outside on the stone first and then move inside to join a second angel, reconciling Matthew with the other Gospels.

discrepancy.note: Strauss notes Mark has the women enter the tomb to find the young man inside, while Matthew's angel never leaves the stone he is seated on outside.

quotes.text: In Mark, who also makes them enter into the grave, they see only one young man in a long white garment, not standing, but sitting on the right side, who gives them the same intelligence. In Matthew they receive this information before they enter into the grave, from the angel, who after rolling away the stone had sat upon it.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846), pt. III, ch. II, on Matthew 28:2 and Mark 16:5.

sides.snippet: an angel of the Lord descended from the sky, and came and rolled away the stone from the door, and sat on it.
sides.verseText: Behold, there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended from the sky, and came and rolled away the stone from the door, and sat on it.

sides.snippet: Entering into the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, dressed in a white robe, and they were amazed.
sides.verseText: Entering into the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, dressed in a white robe, and they were amazed.
